stories.title: Over 5,000 deaths in DRC's deadliest Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: More than 5,000 people have died from the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which began in May and became the country’s deadliest in August. The health ministry reports a current case‑fatality rate of 48.6% and says the epicentre remains in the conflict‑ridden Ituri province in the north‑east, hampering containment.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.

stories.title: Spain high‑speed train crash kills dozens, 69 bodies recovered
stories.summary: A collision on the high‑speed rail line south of Madrid resulted in 69 bodies being recovered from wreckage and an embankment, marking a second major rail disaster in Spain within nine months after a crash near Córdoba that killed 46 people. The incident has eroded public confidence in the rail network and the Socialist‑led government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, and a formal investigation has just been launched.
stories.why: The crash occurs weeks before a snap general election, raising political stakes for the Sánchez government.

stories.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
stories.summary: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile.

stories.title: New India slips into red with 1,267 cr loss in Q2
stories.summary: New India Assurance Company has revealed a concerning net loss of ₹1,267 crore for the September quarter, sharply contrasting with last year's profit of ₹63 crore. Despite this, gross written premiums showed a modest increase of 5.14% year-on-year, totaling ₹11,083 crore.

stories.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
stories.summary: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday. Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips.
